result.title: MemAct: Streaming Spatial Understanding with Memory and Active Exploration
result.summary: Spatial understanding is essential for embodied agents navigating and interacting with the physical world. As observations arrive incrementally, agents must reason in a streaming manner. Yet streaming understanding must also be closed-loop: task-relevant evidence may require both recalling past observations and actively acquiring new views. Existing streaming approaches largely emphasize processing incoming observations, leaving task-driven active exploration underexplored. We introduce MemAct, a framework for streaming spatial understanding with memory and action. A shared vision--language model incrementally writes structured historical memory, retrieves records and past frames on demand, and acquires additional evidence through movement and turning. Retrieved evidence and action observations inform subsequent decisions, enabling the agent to continue exploring or answer within a unified reasoning loop. We develop the MemAct suite, a data generation pipeline and collection across real and simulated environments, with approximately 1M training examples for spatial reasoning, memory writing, retrieval, and exploration. Its MemAct-bench comprises 20,000 main QA pairs evaluating current-observation understanding, historical evidence use, and active exploration, plus 2,000 separate Timing questions. MemAct combines supervised fine-tuning for memory and interaction with counterfactual action optimization using cumulative evidence gains, action costs, and terminal answer quality to improve exploration and stopping decisions. Experiments show that MemAct outperforms existing spatial understanding and streaming baselines and approaches frontier multimodal models on MemAct-bench while retaining streaming inference efficiency.

AI.brief_summary: MemAct 提出一个共享 VLM 的流式空间理解框架：模型增量写入结构化历史记忆、按需检索记录与过去帧，并通过移动、转向主动获取新证据，在统一推理循环中决定继续探索或作答；配套约 1M 训练样例的数据生成管线与含 2 万主 QA、2 千 Timing 问题的 MemAct-bench，并用监督微调加基于累计证据增益、动作成本与终止作答质量的反事实动作优化来改进探索与停止。
AI.relevance_reason: 与 THINK/LOOK/STOP 的收益—成本问题直接相关：记忆写入与检索涉及视觉证据筛选和历史状态保留，主动移动与 Timing 评测涉及何时继续获取证据与停止决策，其反事实动作优化可供核查 LVR 中贡献分配与监督设计；但未涉及 latent 状态生成。
